title: Silver Maple: Ancient Silver Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: A fast, short-lived American river tree that keeps outliving its reputation. Three mapped, from a Den Bosch bastion to a four-trunked Madrid oddity.
intro: Silver maple grows fast, splits easily in a storm, and is usually gone before it turns a hundred, which makes every old one on this list an exception to its own species. Acer saccharinum comes from the flooded river bottoms of eastern North America, where it is built to take a spring deluge that would kill less flexible trees. In Den Bosch it stands with a plane and a lime on a surviving 17th-century bastion, and separately along the old inner-city water at roughly 110 years and 25 metres. In Madrid's walled Cecilio Rodriguez garden one gave up on a single trunk early and grew four. Poznan made its finest specimen, a 105-year-old on Zakrzewski, an official natural monument. Three cities, three very different reasons the tree was allowed to keep going.
